description: The Earth Dog in Chinese astrology: personality, Earth element traits, 1958 and 2018 dates and compatibility.
answer: In Chinese astrology, the Earth Dog is the Dog born in a Earth year, one of five versions of the eleventh animal. It combines the Dog's loyalty with Earth's qualities. Earth Dog years between 1924 and 2044 are 1958 and 2018. The Dog's fixed element is Earth.

sections.heading: The Earth Dog personality
paragraphs: The Dog always carries Earth, so an Earth year doubles its fixed element. Traditional readings describe this as the Dog at its most grounded: dependable, practical, patient and deeply loyal. Earth Dogs are often portrayed as fair-minded, responsible and quietly hardworking, the kind of friend who turns up with practical help in a crisis. They tend to value honesty and consistency above flashier qualities. Doubled Earth gives them extraordinary steadiness. It can also bring worry and pessimism, and readings mention a tendency to brood over problems, resist change and become stubborn when their sense of what is right is challenged. Their affection shows less in words than in a mended fence, a cooked meal or a lift at midnight, and they remember every promise they make.

In classical thought, Earth belongs to the centre and to the late-summer pause between seasons, the point where things ripen and settle. As a year stem, it tends to slow an animal down in a useful way, adding prudence, loyalty and a strong sense of responsibility. People born under an Earth stem are often described as dependable, sensible and protective of the people they love. They value security and tend to build carefully. The caution traditionally attached to Earth is caution itself: overthinking, clinging to the familiar and carrying other people's problems as though they were their own.

sections.heading: Earth Dog at work and in love
paragraphs: At work, Earth is usually associated with management, organisation and long-term stewardship. Earth-year people are often described as the steady hands who keep systems running, look after budgets and notice when colleagues are struggling, which suits administration, property, finance, agriculture, healthcare and operations. They tend to earn trust slowly and keep it. The traditional caution is resistance to change: an Earth stem may hold on to a process after it has stopped working, so regular reviews and a willingness to experiment help.

Steady, fair and practical, the Earth Dog is the dependable backbone many organisations quietly rely on. Facilities management, local government, insurance, school administration and trade associations suit it, since consistency and an honest word are valued there above sparkle. It likes knowing who is responsible for what and will cover a colleague's shift without fuss. Married or partnered, the Earth Dog tends to be patient and sensible, careful with shared money and attentive to elderly relatives and family traditions. It hopes for reliability returned in equal measure. The snag is a pessimistic streak: it may brace for the worst so habitually that a partner's excitement about a new plan meets a list of risks instead of enthusiasm.

sections.heading: Earth Dog years and dates
paragraphs: Between 1924 and 2044 the Earth Dog years are 1958 (February 18, 1958 to February 7, 1959) and 2018 (February 16, 2018 to February 4, 2019). Because the year begins at Lunar New Year, a birthday in January or early February needs checking: in 1958 anyone born before Feb 18 is a Fire Rooster, not a Earth Dog. The combination returns every sixty years, since five elements cycle through twelve animals and only meet the same pairing again after five rounds of the zodiac. Every Earth Dog year is Yang, matching the Dog's own polarity.

Chinese almanacs call the combination Wu-Xu, joining the heavenly stem Wu to the earthly branch Xu. Births just before each new year fall in the Fire Rooster year (before February 18, 1958) and the Fire Rooster year (before February 16, 2018), and births in the weeks after each Earth Dog year ends belong to the Earth Pig. The new year itself fell on a Tuesday in 1958 and Friday in 2018.

sections.heading: Growth edges and compatibility for the Earth Dog
paragraphs: For Earth Dogs, cultivating optimism and flexibility brings the most relief. Noticing worried thoughts and asking what evidence supports them can loosen pessimism's grip. Trying new experiences in small doses keeps doubled Earth from settling into rigidity. Earth Dogs often excel in stewardship roles such as finance, property, care or administration. Because they give steady support to others, they need to ask for support themselves. Lighthearted activities and humour lift their spirits. When steadiness is balanced with openness, Earth Dogs become the bedrock friends and colleagues rely on. A regular hobby done purely for fun, with no duty attached, also helps.

For relationships, the classical structures belong to the animal rather than the element, so the Earth Dog shares the Dog's San He trine with the Tiger and Horse (the Fire trine), its Liu He bond with the Rabbit, and its Liu Chong clash with the Dragon. The element adds a second layer: another Earth sign shares this year element, while partners whose year element feeds Earth in the generating cycle are often described as supportive.

faq.question: What years are Earth Dog years?
faq.answer: Between 1924 and 2044: 1958 (from February 18, 1958) and 2018 (from February 16, 2018). Each lasts until the day before the next Lunar New Year.

faq.question: What is the Earth Dog's element relationship?
faq.answer: The year element is Earth and the Dog's fixed element is Earth; in the five-element cycles earth year element matches the fixed element. Readings use that relationship to describe how easily the two sides of the sign sit together.

faq.question: Which animals are most compatible with the Earth Dog?
faq.answer: Traditionally the Tiger and Horse (San He) and the Rabbit (Liu He). The Dragon is the Liu Chong clash. These pairings depend on the animal, whatever the element.

faq.question: What is the Earth Dog called in the Chinese calendar?
faq.answer: Wu-Xu. In almanacs and Four Pillars charts each year is named by its heavenly stem, here the Earth stem Wu, followed by its earthly branch, here Xu for the Dog, so the name pins down both halves of the combination at once.

faq.question: How is the Earth Dog different from other Dogs?
faq.answer: All Dogs share loyalty, fairness and protectiveness. The Earth year element changes the tone: earth sits at the centre of the five-element wheel, and an Earth year is traditionally said to give any animal steadiness, patience and a practical turn of mind.
